children: a 30% interest in the Bay du Nord project offshore Newfoundland ⁠and Labrador in Canada, while Equinor
will retain a 70% interest and remain as the operator of the project; financial terms were not disclosed.
said the transaction provides an attractive entry point, expected returns above its hurdle rate, and exposure to an established resource base with potential longer-term growth.

The Bay du Nord project is a phased subsea development tied back to a floating production, storage and offloading vessel, with planned gross production capacity of 160K-175K boe/day and first oil anticipated in 2031; it is currently finalizing the front-end engineering and design.
said the deal "supports the continued maturation of Bay du Nord towards ​an investment decision currently ​targeted for early 2027."
